records.claim_text: SAP defines the assigned value for projects as a calculated aggregate, not a single stored field; the page enumerates the exact contributing components.
records.evidence_quote: The assigned value for projects is calculated from:

records.claim_text: Actual costs posted on the budget-carrying WBS element itself count toward that element's assigned value.
records.evidence_quote: Actual costs of WBS element carrying budget

records.claim_text: Statistical actual costs on the budget-carrying WBS element also count toward assigned value, alongside real actual costs.
records.evidence_quote: Statistical actual costs of WBS element carrying budget

records.claim_text: Actual costs of subordinate WBS elements roll into the parent's assigned value only when those subordinates do not themselves carry budget.
records.evidence_quote: Actual costs of subordinate WBS elements if these do not carry budget

records.claim_text: Commitments on the budget-carrying WBS element count toward assigned value, so purchase commitments consume budget before any actual cost posts.
records.evidence_quote: Commitments of WBS element carrying budget

records.claim_text: Commitments of subordinate WBS elements roll up into assigned value only when those subordinates do not carry their own budget.
records.evidence_quote: Commitments of subordinate WBS elements if these do not carry budget

records.claim_text: For assigned networks or orders SAP takes the MAXIMUM of plan versus actual-plus-commitment, not the sum. This is a non-obvious rule worth replicating.
records.evidence_quote: Maximum of plan and actual costs + commitments from assigned networks or orders

records.claim_text: Settlement debits posted to a WBS element increase its assigned value.
records.evidence_quote: Debit from settlement to WBS element

records.claim_text: Settlement credits reduce assigned value only when the receiving object is itself budget-controlled, such as an internal order or WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Credit from settlement to budget-controlled object (internal order, WBS element)

records.claim_text: SAP explicitly lists exclusions from assigned value; the exclusion list is normative, not incidental.
records.evidence_quote: Not used for calculation of the assigned value:

records.claim_text: Cost elements flagged as exempt in availability-control Customizing are excluded from assigned value, giving a configurable carve-out mechanism.
records.evidence_quote: Actual costs with a cost element defined in Customizing for availability control as an exempt cost element

records.claim_text: Costs from business transactions outside the valid business transaction groups of availability control are excluded from assigned value.
records.evidence_quote: Actual costs that resulted from a business transaction that does not belong to the valid business transaction groups of availability control

records.claim_text: Settlement credits to a non-budget-controlled object such as a cost center do NOT reduce assigned value, so settling to a cost center does not free budget.
records.evidence_quote: Credits from settlement to an object that is not budget-controlled (for example, cost center)

records.claim_text: Revenues are excluded from assigned value entirely; budget consumption in SAP PS is a cost-side concept only.
records.evidence_quote: Revenues

records.claim_text: In the budgeting value display SAP gives the compact definition of assigned value as the total of commitment and actual postings, shown only when availability control is active.
records.evidence_quote: Total of commitment and actual postings. The assigned value is only displayed if availability control is active.

records.claim_text: Current budget equals original budget as modified by budget updates, namely supplements, returns and transfers.
records.evidence_quote: Original budget that was changed by budget updates (supplements, returns, and transfers).

records.claim_text: Distributed value is the total of the current budget held by a WBS element's lower-level WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: The total of the current budget (see below) for a WBS element or lower-level WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Distributable value is current budget minus distributed value; this is the amount still available to push down the hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: This is the difference between the current budget and distributed value.

records.claim_text: Cumulated value is the total of the annual budgets, and remaining value is overall budget minus cumulated - the annual-versus-overall reconciliation pair.
records.evidence_quote: Cumulated value Total of the annual budgets.

records.claim_text: The Release value in the budget display is derived from the current budget, confirming release is a subset of current budget rather than an independent amount.
records.evidence_quote: Release Based on the released budget from the current budget

records.claim_text: After supplements, returns or transfers, all derived display values are recomputed from the current budget, never from the frozen original budget.
records.evidence_quote: the displayed values (such as the distributed value) are always based on the current budget, not the original budget.

records.claim_text: Availability control activation behaviour is driven by an Activation Type field on the budget profile, not by a per-transaction switch.
records.evidence_quote: In the budget profile, you use Activation Type to define whether, and how, availability control is to be activated.

records.claim_text: SAP offers exactly three activation types: cannot be activated, automatic activation with budget allocation, and background activation.
records.evidence_quote: 0 = Cannot be activated 1 = Automatic Activation With Budget Allocation 2 = Background Activation

records.claim_text: On activation SAP first determines which WBS elements carry budget; SAP calls these the controlling elements.
records.evidence_quote: Determination of WBS elements carrying budget ("controlling elements")

records.claim_text: Assigned funds checked against a controlling element may sit on that element, on lower-level WBS elements, or on their assigned project orders.
records.evidence_quote: The assigned funds can be on the budget-carrying WBS element, the lower-level WBS elements and their assigned project orders.

records.claim_text: Once availability control is active every posting to the project is checked, making it a synchronous gate on transaction processing.
records.evidence_quote: After activation, each posting to the project is checked by the availability control.

records.claim_text: SAP warns that availability control affects system performance and recommends background activation for less detailed projects - a real cost of always-on checking.
records.evidence_quote: As availability control affects system performance, you should activate it in the background for projects with less detail

records.claim_text: Background activation triggers on a usage level threshold defined in the budget profile; exceeding that usage level activates availability control.
records.evidence_quote: Background activation for availability control checks whether or not the usage level defined in the budget profile has been reached.

records.claim_text: Background activation of availability control writes a log of the objects for which it activated control, enabling audit of when a project became gated.
records.evidence_quote: Background activation of availability control logs the objects for which you activated availability control.

records.claim_text: Online activation lets a user activate availability control for a single project ahead of the usage level being reached or the next batch run.
records.evidence_quote: You can activate availability control for a project before the usage level is reached or before the next batch run.

records.claim_text: Online activation takes effect at the next Save or Check action, after which every posting in the project is checked.
records.evidence_quote: Availability control is activated the next time you choose Save or Check. After activation, every posting in the project is checked

records.claim_text: The budget profile determines both whether availability control activates and which budget values it checks against.
records.evidence_quote: whether/how availability control is to be activated and which budget values should be checked by availability control.

records.claim_text: Availability control can be configured against year-independent total values or year-dependent annual values, a fundamental modelling fork.
records.evidence_quote: year-independent (= total values) or year-dependent values.

records.claim_text: SAP splits availability control into a passive mode giving an overview of funds and their assignment, and an active mode that blocks over-assignment.
records.evidence_quote: Overview of funds, their assignment and type

records.claim_text: Active availability control exists to prevent the assignment of too many funds, checking remaining budget as business transactions create costs.
records.evidence_quote: Prevents the assignment of too many funds

records.claim_text: SAP defines distributable budget as the controlling element's budget not yet distributed to lower-level WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: The budget from the controlling element that is _not_ yet distributed to other, lower-level WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Availability control controls costs actively by issuing warnings and error messages at the moment costs are incurred.
records.evidence_quote: control costs actively by issuing warnings and error messages when costs are incurred.

records.claim_text: Tolerance limits are keyed on a three-part combination of budget profile, transaction group and action, and may be expressed as relative or absolute variance.
records.evidence_quote: You can define relative or absolute variance from budget values as tolerance limits for budget profile/transaction group/action combinations.

records.claim_text: If no tolerance limit is found for a posting, SAP permits the posting - the control is opt-in and fails open, not closed.
records.evidence_quote: If no tolerance limit is found, the posting is permitted.

records.claim_text: Action 1 is a pure warning: the user is told the tolerance limit is exceeded but the posting is not rejected.
records.evidence_quote: The system informs you that the tolerance limit is being exceeded. However, the posting in question is not rejected.

records.claim_text: Action 3 is a hard stop: a posting that breaches the action-3 tolerance limit is rejected and an error message is generated.
records.evidence_quote: If a posting leads to the action 3 tolerance limit being exceeded, the system rejects the posting and generates an error message.

records.claim_text: The middle action tier is warning plus mail, notifying a responsible manager rather than only the posting user. Documented on the Funds Management action page.
records.evidence_quote: Warning with Mail to funds center manager

records.claim_text: Every business transaction is assigned to a transaction group for availability control, and tolerance limits are set per group.
records.evidence_quote: All business transactions are assigned to a transaction group in availability control.

records.claim_text: An all-transaction-groups catch-all exists so tolerance limits need not be defined for every group individually; specific groups override the catch-all.
records.evidence_quote: simplifies entry and is useful if you do _not_ want to define separate tolerance limits for every transaction group.

records.claim_text: Budgeting itself is a transaction group, which lets availability control react to retrospective budget reductions made during a running project.
records.evidence_quote: Budgeting: Enables availability control to account for retrospective budget changes during projects

records.claim_text: A user status can exclude a budgeted WBS element and its lower-level assignment elements from availability control.
records.evidence_quote: You can exclude a WBS element with budget and the lower-level account assignment elements from availability control.

records.claim_text: When excluded by status, assigned funds trigger no availability-control action, yet assigned values continue to be updated on the controlling element.
records.evidence_quote: the assigned funds are not included in the availability control, in other words, no action is triggered. However, the assigned values are still updated

records.claim_text: SAP states budget allocation is generally preceded by a cost plan which forms the initial basis for determining and allocating the budget.
records.evidence_quote: Budget allocation for a project or an order is generally preceded by a cost plan that provides the initial basis for determination and allocation

records.claim_text: SAP's learning material draws the key distinction: the budget is the approved cost framework and differs from the cost plan by being binding.
records.evidence_quote: The budget is the approved cost framework for a project. It differs from the cost plan in that it is binding.

records.claim_text: Plan values can be copied into budget by selecting WBS elements carrying the plan values, applying a chosen percentage of plan total.
records.evidence_quote: Select the WBS elements that contain the plan values you want to use as the budget

records.claim_text: The budget profile controls the period of time during which budgeting is allowed - a time-window gate on the budgeting activity itself.
records.evidence_quote: The period of time during which budgeting is allowed

records.claim_text: The budget profile also determines whether budgeting is permitted for total values, annual values, or both.
records.evidence_quote: Whether budgeting is allowed for total annual values, and/or annual values

records.claim_text: Budget may be allocated once the object has reached status Created; a user status can be defined to restrict this further.
records.evidence_quote: You can allocate budget after the status Created has been reached.

records.claim_text: A supplement posts additional budget to a receiver WBS element for a stated receiver year, which is the year the receiver gains additional budget.
records.evidence_quote: The Receiver year is the year in which the receiver object receives additional budget.

records.claim_text: A Total values too indicator makes the supplement change the receiver's total budget by the same amount as the annual values, keeping the two layers in sync.
records.evidence_quote: the system changes the total budget for the receiver to the same extent as the annual values.

records.claim_text: Supplement entry supports Hold, Check and Post; Check reports errors before posting and erroneous rows are excluded from the post.
records.evidence_quote: You can use the checking function before posting to determine whether the entered items contain any errors.

records.claim_text: A budget return is entered against a sender WBS element and an amount, mirroring the supplement flow but reducing budget.
records.evidence_quote: entering the sender WBS element and the amount

records.claim_text: Budget transfers move budget between different WBS elements in the same period, and SAP also supports transfers across periods and years.
records.evidence_quote: Transfers between different WBS elements in the same period

records.claim_text: When budgeting in object currency, transfers made in other currencies do not appear as entered values at higher hierarchy levels though current budget includes them.
records.evidence_quote: transfers made in other currencies are not displayed as an entered value in objects from higher hierarchy levels

records.claim_text: The budget Check function runs both consistency checks and availability control checks in one action.
records.evidence_quote: The Check function executes both consistency checks and availability control checks.

records.claim_text: The consistency rule is that the summed budget of lower-level WBS elements must not exceed the budget of the level above.
records.evidence_quote: the budget values of a lower-level of the WBS element (distributed values) exceed the budget value of the level above

records.claim_text: SAP warns that totals matching annual values in one currency can still diverge in controlling area or object currency - a rounding and translation trap.
records.evidence_quote: Even if the total values match the annual values in a defined currency, the values in the controlling area or object currency can differ.

records.claim_text: Budget is distributed top-down from the total budget to individual WBS elements, and may be entered directly on WBS elements when plan values are unsuitable.
records.evidence_quote: Distribute the total budget (using the top-down method) to the individual elements.

records.claim_text: SAP does not support reassigning a WBS element that carries budget within the work breakdown structure - a hard structural constraint.
records.evidence_quote: Reassigning a WBS element (that has a budget) within the work breakdown structure is not supported

records.claim_text: The Total Up function overwrites a WBS element's budget value with the value actually distributed to its children, a downward-driven roll-up.
records.evidence_quote: overwrites a budget value on a WBS element with the distributed value (roll-up).

records.claim_text: Total Up exists because in decentralized budgeting the person responsible for the overall budget needs an overview of the sectional budgets.
records.evidence_quote: the person responsible for the overall budget requires an overview of the sectional budgets.

records.claim_text: Allocating budget to a WBS element for the first time sets the system status budgeted, which persists even if the budget is later removed.
records.evidence_quote: the system status budgeted is set.

records.claim_text: The budgeted status blocks deletion of WBS elements and reassignment of the element and all subordinate objects.
records.evidence_quote: Deletion of WBS elements

records.claim_text: The budgeted status can only be removed when budget was removed using the same transaction that allocated it and the selected WBS elements have budget zero.
records.evidence_quote: The budget is removed using the same transaction with which it was allocated and The selected WBS elements have budget 0.

records.claim_text: Every saved budgeting change is documented by the system as a line item, giving budget a full audit trail.
records.evidence_quote: Each change that you save in budgeting is documented as a line item by the system.

records.claim_text: Line item writing can be suppressed for original budget changes via user status, but line items are always written for budget updates.
records.evidence_quote: You can prohibit line item writing for changes to the original budget by means of a user status

records.claim_text: Each budget line item is stored in the currency in which it was entered, which SAP calls the budgeting currency.
records.evidence_quote: Each budget line item is saved in the currency in which you entered it (budgeting currency).

records.claim_text: SAP advises keeping exchange rates stable and specifically not changing them while entering the original budget, because retranslation distorts comparisons.
records.evidence_quote: Keep the exchange rates as stable as possible. In particular, you should _not_ change the exchange rates while entering the original budget.

records.claim_text: Budget carryforward moves budget remainders from projects, internal orders and plant maintenance orders into the following fiscal year.
records.evidence_quote: The budget carryforward enables you to carry forward budget remainders from projects, internal orders, and plant maintenance orders to the following fiscal year.

records.claim_text: Unused budget for carryforward is defined as planned budget minus incurred actual costs - notably a different base than assigned value.
records.evidence_quote: A budget that has _not_ been used up is mainly defined here as the difference between planned budget and incurred actual costs.

records.claim_text: Commitments are excluded from the unused-budget calculation, so commitment carryforward must be executed before budget carryforward.
records.evidence_quote: Commitments are not taken into account when the _unused_ budget is calculated.

records.claim_text: There is no availability control during budget carryforward, so the carryforward run itself cannot be blocked by tolerance limits.
records.evidence_quote: There is _no_ availability control during the budget carryforward.

records.claim_text: Carryforward is permitted only for objects with status Created, Released or Technically completed, and is blocked for Closed or deletion-flagged objects.
records.evidence_quote: Budget carryforward is only allowed if the object (WBS element/internal order) has been Created, Released, or Technically completed.

records.claim_text: Negative budget cannot be carried forward into the following year.
records.evidence_quote: You _cannot_ carry forward negative budget into the following year.

records.claim_text: Carryforward is repeatable and idempotent by design: repeat runs pick up only budgets excluded from earlier runs, and it supports test and update modes.
records.evidence_quote: You can carry forward budget more than once in a row.

records.claim_text: Follow-up postings of actual costs cause the system to post carried-forward budget back, capped at the total budget carried forward.
records.evidence_quote: If you make follow-up postings of actual costs, the system posts back budget that was carried forward to the following year

records.claim_text: In S/4HANA Cloud the budget availability control profile bundles time range, cost items as semantic tags, tolerance limits for budget usage, and the requested system response.
records.evidence_quote: you specify the time range of the budget, the cost items (as relevant semantic tags), the tolerance limits for budget usage

records.claim_text: Time Range decides whether budget is treated as a yearly or an overall budget for projects and WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: The Time Range defines whether the budget is considered as a yearly budget or an overall budget for projects and WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Selecting Overall Budget compares posted costs against a project overall budget that may span more than one fiscal year.
records.evidence_quote: If you select Overall Budget, the posted costs are compared with the overall budget of a project, which could span more than one fiscal year.

records.claim_text: Selecting Annual Budget compares posted costs against the project's annual budget within the related fiscal year only.
records.evidence_quote: If you select Annual Budget, the posted costs are compared with the annual budget of a project within the related fiscal year.

records.claim_text: Tolerance limits are expressed as budget usage rates maintained per activity group, each carrying an assigned message type.
records.evidence_quote: The Tolerance Limits for the budget usage rates are maintained for each activity group.

records.claim_text: A warning-type tolerance limit still allows budget to be used after the limit is exceeded - warnings are advisory only.
records.evidence_quote: If you assign a warning to a budget tolerance limit, the budget can still be used even after the tolerance limit has been exceeded.

records.claim_text: An error-type tolerance limit blocks the posting of commitments such as purchase orders or purchase requisitions once exceeded.
records.evidence_quote: the system responds with an error message and commitments, such as purchase orders or purchase requisitions, can't be posted.

records.claim_text: The catch-all activity group All Activity Groups is mandatory in every budget availability control profile, configured with either a warning or an error message type.
records.evidence_quote: In a budget availability control profile, the activity group All Activity Groups (++) is mandatory.

records.claim_text: A specific activity group's usage rate is checked when configured; otherwise the All Activity Groups rate applies by default.
records.evidence_quote: Otherwise, the usage rate for activity group All Activity Groups (++) is used by default.

records.claim_text: Per semantic tag you specify budget usage rates at which a first notification and further notifications are sent - a stepped alerting model.
records.evidence_quote: For each semantic tag, you can specify budget usage rates at which a first notification and further notifications are sent.

records.claim_text: The threshold fields are named % of Budget Used before First Notification and % Increment for Further Notifications.
records.evidence_quote: % of Budget Used before First Notification % Increment for Further Notifications

records.claim_text: SAP's project financial reporting surfaces Budget, Project Stock, Actual Cost, Commitment, Assigned Value and Available Budget as distinct displayed measures.
records.evidence_quote: correctly displays the Budget, Project Stock, Actual Cost, Commitment, Assigned Value, and Available Budget in Global Currency.

records.claim_text: Budget Currency Type for availability control is either Global Currency or Project Currency, and budget data must exist in the selected type.
records.evidence_quote: You can select either Global Currency or Project Currency. However, you must ensure that budget data is available in the currency type that you select.

records.claim_text: Budget availability control spans the whole lifecycle: it starts at budget maintenance, runs on each commitment and actual cost posting, and ends at cost-versus-budget analysis.
records.evidence_quote: starts with the budget maintenance process, runs with each commitment posting and actual cost posting, and ends with the analysis of costs and budget.

records.claim_text: Warning-with-mail actions fail when no manager name is entered on the WBS element or project definition - the notification target is master data, not config.
records.evidence_quote: no manager name has been entered in the WBS element, or in the project definition

records.claim_text: Absence of any availability control message means either control is not active or no tolerance limit has been exceeded - silence is ambiguous.
records.evidence_quote: This indicates availability control isn't active or tolerance limits haven't been exceeded.

records.claim_text: SAP ships a dedicated monitor comparing budget and assigned values for WBS elements in real time, reachable via transaction IM_AVCHANA_WBS.
records.evidence_quote: drill down according to the characteristics in this layout

records.claim_text: Overall planning plans project costs hierarchically in the WBS, per element, either yearly or as a single overall value.
records.evidence_quote: You can plan the cost of each WBS element on a yearly basis or plan using the overall value.

records.claim_text: Projects can be planned in controlling area currency, object currency, or transaction currency, configured through the planning profile.
records.evidence_quote: Projects can be planned in the controlling area currency, object currency, or transaction currency

records.claim_text: The first cost planning run for a project automatically creates version 0, which is the leading plan version.
records.evidence_quote: The first time you run cost planning for a project, this automatically creates version 0.

records.claim_text: Transfer of Easy Cost Planning from an appropriation request to a project or WBS element always occurs in the leading CO version, not an alternative version.
records.evidence_quote: Transferring ECP from an appropriation request to a project or WBS element always occurs in the leading CO version.

records.claim_text: Overall planning is the simplest cost planning type; cost element planning is used when detailed information exists at a more advanced project stage.
records.evidence_quote: when you have detailed information available, normally at a more advanced stage of a project

records.claim_text: Manual cost planning captures the costs, activities and business processes expected to occur during the project, per WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: enter the costs, activities, and business processes you expect to occur during your project for the WBS element.

records.claim_text: Structure-oriented overall planning is neither by cost element nor period-specific, making it suitable only for a first rough estimate.
records.evidence_quote: neither by cost element nor is it period-specific

records.claim_text: SAP positions overall planning as suitable for a simple first rough estimate of costs for the project and its work packages.
records.evidence_quote: is suitable for a simple, first (rough) estimate of the costs for the project and its work packages.

records.claim_text: Availability control checks against the budget while taking assigned funds into account, confirming assigned value is the consumption side of the comparison.
records.evidence_quote: checks against the budget, taking assigned funds into account.

records.claim_text: Budgets must be distributed consistently within the project structure; consistency is a first-class rule, not a report-time nicety.
records.evidence_quote: must be distributed consistently

records.claim_text: SAP treats distributing a budget as distinct from releasing the funds, which is why a separate release layer exists at all.
records.evidence_quote: In many organizations, distributing a budget is not the same as releasing the funds allocated to it.

records.claim_text: In SAP's Budget Control System a release is based on the current total budget and may be done all at once or periodically. Note: this page documents Funds Management, not PS.
records.evidence_quote: A release is based on the current total budget, which you can release at one time. You can also release your budget periodically.

records.claim_text: Statistical orders or WBS elements permit planning and budget monitoring without allowing settlement, giving a monitor-only budget object pattern.
records.evidence_quote: planning and budget monitoring

records.claim_text: Active availability checks prevent posting of transactions that would exceed the budget, based on tolerance limits configured in budget profiles.
records.evidence_quote: prevent posting of transactions that would exceed the budget

records.claim_text: INFERENCE: available budget equals the checked budget basis (current or released, overall or annual) minus assigned value. SAP never prints this formula on one page.
records.evidence_quote: whether/how availability control is to be activated and which budget values should be checked by availability control.

records.claim_text: INFERENCE: the current budget basis for availability control is composed of original budget plus supplement, less return, plus repostings from the budget.
records.evidence_quote: Original Budget Supplement Return Repostings from the Budget

records.claim_text: For projects specifically, availability control can be configured to check against the released budget rather than the current budget.
records.evidence_quote: For projects: can check against current or released budget

records.claim_text: SAP's budgeting components support both top-down and bottom-up budget principles, so a design must not assume one direction only.
records.evidence_quote: top-down principle or the bottom-up principle

records.claim_text: SAP budgeting supports overall budgets or annual budgets depending on how funds are used, and the two coexist rather than being alternatives.
records.evidence_quote: overall budgets or annual budgets

records.claim_text: Annual budget distribution can be driven either per WBS element across years, or by fixing a year and budgeting all WBS elements for that year.
records.evidence_quote: budget all WBS elements for a certain year

records.claim_text: Copy view, revaluate and total up functions are all available when budgeting annual values, not only for overall values.
records.evidence_quote: The Copy view, reevaluate, and Total up functions are also available for budgeting annual values

records.claim_text: Plan total sums structure planning, cost element planning, unit costing, additive assigned orders and additive networks or activities across the element and its subordinates.
records.evidence_quote: Structure planning value (independent of cost element) + Cost element planning value + Unit costing value
